newsitem.title: USA: NAVISTAR IN DIESEL ENGINE PACT WITH FORD. [CORRECTED 17:40 GMT]
newsitem.headline: NAVISTAR IN DIESEL ENGINE PACT WITH FORD. [CORRECTED 17:40 GMT]

text.p: Ford Motor Co and Navistar International Corp said Wednesday they have reached tentative agreement for Navistar to continue to supply diesel engines for Ford's over 8500-lb GVW F-Series trucks and Econoline vans.

Under the tentative terms, Navistar will produce a newly designed and advanced technology engine for Ford. The new 10- year agreement would be effective beginning with model year 2003, according to a joint statement.
The proposed agreement requires approval by directors of both companies.
Navistar has made engines for Ford since 1982, a Navistar spokeswoman said.

In 1997, Navistar expects to provide Ford with 178,000 diesel engines (corrects from 220,000 diesel engines) for Econoline vans and heavy pickup trucks, the spokeswoman said, adding that Ford accounts for 90 percent of the company's V-8 engine business.
She said Navistar does not know how many of the new diesel engines it will sell to Ford.
Navistar shares were up 9/16 at 21-1/8 Wednesday.
